chunks: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah narrated from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, he raised it (to the Imam), he said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Commanding the good and forbidding the evil are two characteristics of the characteristics of Allah, the Exalted. Whoever supports them, Allah will honor him; and whoever abandons them, Allah will abandon him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of supporting or abandoning the practice of commanding good and forbidding evil?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elevates 'commanding the good and forbidding the evil' from a mere legal obligation to a fundamental divine attribute (*khuluq*), emphasizing that Allah's honor and abandonment are directly contingent upon human adherence to this practice. This framing underscores the concept of *tashabbuh* (resemblance) to God, where believers actualize divine mercy and justice in the community, a core tenet in Shia jurisprudence and ethics.
